themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Chaos Erupts
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints spiked 833% THIS WEEK (7 complaints vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks), suggesting rapid expansion of sidewalk seating, encroachments, or enforcement gaps in Greenpoint/Williamsburg's restaurant scene.
evidence: 7 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 average per week over prior 8 weeks (833% spike, z-score 5.74)
Spike is statistically significant and highly recent, indicating sudden change in last 7 days
Hell Gate just published positive coverage of Greenpoint dining scene (April 16), suggesting recent restaurant activity uptick
reporting_angles: Are restaurants illegally expanding sidewalk seating without permits post-pandemic?
Which blocks are seeing the most complaints—map the hotspots and visit them during peak hours

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deteriorating Rapidly
themes_detail.summary: Street sign failures (missing and dangling signs) spike 243-264% THIS WEEK and LAST WEEK (11 total complaints over 2 weeks vs. 3.2 weekly average), plus dead/dying trees up 367% THIS WEEK (7 complaints vs. 1.5 avg), signaling accelerating street maintenance neglect.
evidence: Street Sign - Missing: 5 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 avg (264% spike, z-score 5.21)
Street Sign - Dangling: 6 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.8 avg (243% spike, z-score 3.9)
Dead/Dying Tree: 7 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 avg (367% spike, z-score 3.89)
Community Board has repeatedly requested park/amenity reconstruction and DOT traffic calming—suggests long-standing neglect now accelerating
reporting_angles: Interview DOT and Parks Dept about staffing cuts or maintenance backlog—why are signs and trees failing simultaneously?
Walk the district and photograph missing/dangling street signs; map them to specific blocks for visual story

themes_detail.label: Vendor and Park Enforcement Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints surge 500% THIS WEEK (9 vs. 1.5 weekly average) and park noise complaints jump 460% THIS WEEK (7 vs. 1.2 avg), suggesting either aggressive street vending expansion or sudden enforcement action causing resident backlash.
evidence: Vendor Enforcement: 9 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 avg (500% spike, z-score 4.16)
Noise - Park: 7 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 avg (460% spike, z-score 4.13)
Both spikes are this week only, indicating sudden, coordinated change in street/park activity or enforcement posture
reporting_angles: Did the city announce or execute a new street vending crackdown this week? Interview vendors and enforcement officers.
Which parks saw noise complaints—is there a specific concert, event, or seasonal reopening driving the spike?

themes_detail.label: Panhandling and Transit Disorder Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints surged 260% TWO WEEKS AGO (9 vs. 2.5 weekly average) and taxi complaints jumped 433% TWO WEEKS AGO (4 vs. 0.8 avg), suggesting emerging disorder issues or changes in street activity that may be ongoing.
evidence: Panhandling: 9 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 2.5 avg (260% spike, z-score 4.33)
Taxi Complaint: 4 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.8 avg (433% spike, z-score 3.92)
Community Board has standing request for homeless services, suggesting prior awareness of disorder issues; current spike may represent escalation
Both spikes occurred 2 weeks ago; unclear if sustained or resolved
reporting_angles: Are recent weather changes or transit service changes driving increased panhandling visibility?
Interview residents and business owners about what changed in street activity mid-April

themes_detail.label: Sustained Parking and Noise Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking dominates 311 calls (4,590 complaints over 90 days) and noise complaints across residential, commercial, and street/sidewalk categories total 4,334 complaints, representing long-running systemic issues that community board budgets request DOT traffic calming to address.
evidence: Illegal Parking: 4,590 complaints over 90 days (51.2 complaints/day, far exceeding any other category)
Noise complaints combined (residential, commercial, street, park, other): 4,334 complaints over 90 days
Community Board repeatedly requests DOT traffic calming and improved pedestrian safety, indicating residents see these as connected priority issues
1,264 building permits filed in 90 days (development pressure) likely exacerbating both parking and noise
reporting_angles: Profile 2-3 Greenpoint/Williamsburg residents dealing with daily illegal parking and noise—how has it changed their quality of life?
Investigate whether rapid development (1,264 permits filed) is overwhelming neighborhood infrastructure; interview DOT about traffic calming plans
